headline: Highest risk is AutoGen’s writable, networked code-execution surface; the zoomcamp profile is non-runnable, so interaction risks are mostly one-way and compliance/data leakage remain limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can ingest files and stdin/stdout and execute role-based tool calls, so prompt injection is plausible if B’s content is manually bridged into A. The zoomcamp profile is non-runnable and exposes no shared channel, so there is no documented default bridge between them; uncertainty keeps this above none but below medium.
conditions: IF an operator copies B-derived text into AutoGen prompts or files
IF AutoGen is configured to parse untrusted course material as instructions
mitigations: Keep B content out of AutoGen prompts unless quoted as data
Add a fixed system prompt that treats imported text as untrusted
Use a separate staging file for B-derived content
Review any tool-call output before execution

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen can read and write configured working directories and may handle model-provider API keys, while the zoomcamp profile has no IO surfaces or data classes touched. With no shared workspace documented and B non-runnable, leakage is not evidenced as a default pairwise path; the remaining risk is limited to operator-created file sharing.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory
IF sensitive files are placed in a directory AutoGen can read
mitigations: Use separate directories for A and B
Remove secrets from shared folders before running A
Mount read-only inputs for AutoGen where possible
Rotate any exposed API keys after testing

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has shell, subprocess, filesystem write, and broad network egress; B has no runtime capability and is marked non-runnable. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely in the default pair, but if an operator maps B artifacts into the same directory, AutoGen could overwrite them; uncertainty does not justify none.
conditions: IF B artifacts are stored in the same writable directory used by AutoGen
IF AutoGen is allowed to modify files that B also consumes
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Disable AutoGen write access for shared folders
Snapshot files before running AutoGen
Avoid concurrent edits to the same path

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate tool calls and code, but B is a course repository/profile with no execution surface, so there is no documented downstream action chain from B into A. The main cascade would require an operator to treat B-derived text as authoritative input to AutoGen, which is not default behavior here.
conditions: IF B output is manually fed into AutoGen as authoritative instructions
IF AutoGen is then permitted to execute resulting tool calls without review
mitigations: Require human review of any B-derived instructions
Separate factual extraction from action execution
Log and inspect AutoGen tool calls before running them
Use a verification step before acting on generated outputs

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model-provider API keys and can touch application data, while B is a public open-source course with no stated regulated data handling. There is no evidence of residency or certification mismatch between them, so compliance risk is limited to accidental placement of regulated data into AutoGen’s workspace.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into AutoGen’s working directory
IF the operator expects B to enforce residency or retention controls
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of AutoGen runs
Document retention for any files AutoGen writes
Use a separate environment for sensitive workloads
Confirm no PHI/PII is stored in shared folders
